notes.name: AIM-120, not the original's "AMRAAM": real_weapons.gd keys its own AMRAAM figures on that name
notes.model: the original's file name, which Models: Detailed draws as our AIM-120 (shared/util/gltf.gd STORES: shared/extra/models/stores/aim120.glb); the F-35I carries it inside its bays, shown while their doors are open
notes.generation: 4: the C-7 is in service after 1995 (weapons.ibx's generation 4)
notes.power: one hit destroys a fighter (inferred, as the AIM-9M)
notes.blast_m: the lethal radius is open; blast scaling (inferred): the AIM-9A / B's 9 m (ds-aim9) for its 4.5 kg warhead times the cube root of this warhead's mass ratio (20 kg)
notes.drag: carriage drag index (10^4 x the drag coefficient on the F-16's 300 sq ft wing, flight-model.md §9.18): 0.4 x its 0.178 m across (w-aim120) frontal area, 0.4 the drag of a finned missile on its launcher rail on that area (inferred); the F-16 manual's published indices were not at hand; none in the F-35I's bays (loadout::sim_load)
notes.motion._absAcceleration: 120 m/s², the AIM-9M record's (inferred: no burn time published)
notes.motion.burn: the burn with which the motion flies the published range from 250 m/s before its flight ends 6 s after the burn (missile.rs real_burn)
notes.motion._timeAcceleration: the burn, so the original's reading of the section flies as long
notes.motion._timeConstOrientation: flies straight 0.5 s after launch (the AIM-9M record's)
notes.motion._dragScale: times the generic missile drag curve (missile.rs CD0): fitted so the AIM-120 flies its 90 km head-on 12,000 m up, the same for every body (docs/real-weapons.md §2.1)
notes.motion._motorThrust: 51.3 kg of propellant at 265 s specific impulse over 7.75 s (iasg-aim120's figures)
notes.motion._maxTime: no public figure; the flight ends by its speed first (inferred: 120 s)
notes.motion._maxG: 35 g, a Korean comparison table quoted in a forum (weak; other posts 28-40 g)
notes.motion._decoyReject: 0.8 (inferred): an active pulse-Doppler seeker tells the chaff from a jet moving along its line of sight, so only a jet on the beam is lost in it (w-chaff); the share is ours (docs/real-weapons.md 2.3)

footnotes.w-aim120: Wikipedia, "AIM-120 AMRAAM" (AIM-120C-5/6/7: 356 lb, 161.5 kg; 12 ft, 3.65 m; 7 in, 0.178 m across; warhead 44 lb, 20 kg; Mach 4; AIM-120C 49 nmi, 90 km) (read 2026-11-10), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIM-120_AMRAAM
footnotes.ds-aim9: designation-systems.net, "Raytheon AIM-9 Sidewinder" (AIM-9A / B effective kill radius about 9 m), https://www.designation-systems.net/dusrm/m-9.html
footnotes.iasg-aim120: T. Tyrell, C. Funk, N. Marton, "AIM-120C-5 Performance Assessment for Digital Combat Simulation Enhancement", revision 2, September 2014 (a hobbyist CFD study: 51.26 kg propellant, 265 s specific impulse, 7.75 s burn; a straight shot from Mach 0.83 5 km up reaches about 35 km), https://www.generalstaff.org/BBOW/Progs/FlySIM/AIM120C5-Performance-Assessment-rev2.pdf
footnotes.wt-aim120: War Thunder forum, "The AIM-120 'AMRAAM' - History, Design, Performance & Discussion" (a Korean comparison table: G-limit 35 for the AIM-120B; others 28-40 g), https://forum.warthunder.com/t/the-aim-120-amraam-history-design-performance-discussion/2584
footnotes.w-chaff: Wikipedia, "Chaff (countermeasure)" (Doppler radars tell the slowing chaff from a jet; on the beam the jet is "more difficult to separate from the effectively stationary chaff") (read 2026-11-22), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaff_(countermeasure)
